home.introduction: Elaina Theme is a Pengu Loader theme for the League Client. It changes the client visuals, adds custom assets, provides wallpaper/audio controls, and includes optional quality-of-life plugins.
features: Image/video wallpaper and background audio with Home media controls.
Local/Google fonts, custom avatar/border/banner/currency/rank/rune/champion art and layout controls.
Active optional helpers: Auto Accept toolbar, Loot Helper, Invite all friends, profile/status display and Name Spoofer.
Offline JSON backup/restore and separately consent-gated cloud/icon services.
Developer MCP integration: 16 upstream tools plus console/network capture, gated by Dev-mode and MCP-enabled.
Legacy Auto Queue/Dodge/practice/skip-honor code remains in source but is not started by the current entrypoint.
configurationModel: Use League Settings -> Elaina theme -> one of four tabs: Theme Settings, Plugins Settings, Backup & Restore, About Us. With the old loader menu enabled, choose Settings from its quick menu first.
ElainaData uses ./data/ElainaData.json when context.fs is available; otherwise it uses the ElainaTheme DataStore entry. Version alone does not prove file operations are usable.
MCP port/token/export configuration lives only in mcp-server/config.local.json; it is separate from theme settings and portable backups.
Follow specific restart prompts for startup-dependent changes. Font mode, volume, activity-center positioning, capture settings and PluginFS list discovery can apply without a restart.
This documentation was checked against source and the Pengu 1.1.6 renderer on 2026-11-15; PluginFS/macOS capabilities are source-backed.

installation.introduction: Install a built release inside the Pengu plugins directory. Theme settings support both DataStore-only installations and context.fs installations; MCP file editing additionally checks version and usable PluginFS methods.
requirements: League Client installed and able to launch normally.
An Elaina Theme release zip or a local build output from this repository.
A writable Pengu Loader plugins folder.
Node.js 20+ and npm only if you want the developer MCP service; the normal theme does not launch a Node listener.

quickGuide.warning: Install the built plugin folder with index.js at its root; do not copy the TypeScript source checkout as a release.

folderLayout: The theme root contains built index.js, assets, config, locales and the independent mcp-server package.
The local helper package elaina-theme-data may also be included by a local build; normal mode selects the configured CDN, Dev-mode selects local helpers.
Use the in-theme Open folder actions so scoped/renamed folders resolve correctly.

MCP config.local.json and installed node_modules are created locally and excluded from the release. Source deployment preserves those and data/, but can replace/delete custom files placed only in installed assets.
afterInstall: Open the League settings gear. If Elaina quick settings appears first, choose Settings to open the full dialog.
Find Elaina theme; review Theme Settings, Plugins Settings, Backup & Restore and About Us.
Configure fonts/media/layout and follow only the restart prompts associated with changes.
For MCP, unlock developer tools with 20 logo clicks, enable Dev-mode, reopen Settings, open its server folder, run the launcher and enable MCP separately.

themeCustomization.introduction: Theme Settings and Plugins Settings follow the current in-client section order. Native labels follow Theme-language with English fallback. Stored keys can outlive controls; legacy keys are documented separately.

assets.introduction: Place files in the installed theme asset folders. File discovery is on demand with usable PluginFS; without it, register basenames manually. No permanent background scan or directory watcher is currently active.

legacySteps: Copy the file into the matching installed theme folder, preserving basename and lowercase extension.
Open Elaina theme -> Theme Settings -> Asset library and expand the row.
Enter the exact basename including extension, such as my-wallpaper.webm, and use Add.
Delete removes a filename from the list, not the physical file.
If Home controls were already built, leave/return Home or reload to rebuild them. Restart does not replace manual filename registration.
pluginFsSteps: Copy the file into the correct installed asset folder. Developers who rebuild should keep the custom file in source assets too.
Open or reopen Theme Settings; its builder awaits refreshLists before rendering.
Alternatively press the Home wallpaper dropdown; its mouse handler scans all four asset lists, including audio.
Choose new wallpaper/audio with Home controls, or banner/font in Settings. Changed media lists rebuild visible controls once.
No client restart is needed for this discovery path; if Settings stayed open, reopen it to rebuild existing labels/options.
rules: Current fileRegex checks lowercase extensions. An accepted extension still needs a renderer-supported codec.
Use unique basenames, not full paths, for manual registration.
No 1-second polling, 30-second polling or filesystem watcher is present; refresh is triggered by startup and relevant UI interaction.
Parallel directory listings and concurrent refresh requests share work; failed reads preserve existing lists.
Do not overwrite local configuration or media when extracting a release. A source deploy preserves runtime data/MCP config/dependencies, but installed-only assets may be removed.
Google Fonts uses HTTPS fonts.googleapis.com/css or /css2 links. Local/Google modes are exclusive and switching updates the owned font stylesheet immediately.

themeCustomization.themeSettingsIntroduction: Current order: General, Asset library, Wallpaper, Audio, Updates and notifications, Custom assets, Interface and layout, Profile and identity, Game tabs and content. Playback saves changed positions on navigation/pause/pagehide; WallpaperAudio-timeUpdate remains a visible legacy input with no scheduling effect.

themeSettingGroups.title: General and language
themeSettingGroups.description: Header tracking switch and Theme-language. Consent/API prerequisites are described in FAQ; there is no Setup/privacy tab in this build.

themeSettingGroups.title: Asset library
themeSettingGroups.description: Manual registration shown without PluginFS. Runtime media lists are not part of the root-default portable backup.

themeSettingGroups.title: Wallpaper
themeSettingGroups.description: Volume, speed, old controls, slideshow, disable and window effects. Window effects are shown when theme wallpaper is disabled and require supported Pengu/OS APIs.

themeSettingGroups.title: Audio and media state
themeSettingGroups.description: Settings contains volume, pause-in-game and disable. Home holds loop/pause/mute/previous/next/progress. Odd pause counters mean paused; even means playing. In-game behavior pauses both audio/video.

themeSettingGroups.title: Custom assets
themeSettingGroups.description: Local replacement and peer download are separate from own-icon upload consent. Expand Custom Icon for its nested switches.

themeSettingGroups.title: Profile and identity
themeSettingGroups.description: Local display values do not grant currency/levels/rank. Custom font is immediate; other startup features may show restart prompts.

themeSettingGroups.title: Game tabs and content
themeSettingGroups.description: These switches only affect matching League renderer elements. Legacy TFT subpages may be absent when TFT uses a separate client.

themeCustomization.pluginSettingsIntroduction: Current Plugins Settings contains core, profile/identity, unlocked developer tools and Dev-mode-only MCP. Queue automation is commented out and not a current UI section. Expand profile rows for details.

pluginSettingGroups.title: Auto Accept matchmaking controls
pluginSettingGroups.description: Activity switch and delay are in the ready-check/matchmaking toolbar; they do not auto-create queues.

pluginSettingGroups.title: Profile and identity plugins
pluginSettingGroups.description: Includes Classic rank controls. Custom Status without Local updates LCU chat and may be visible to friends.

pluginSettingGroups.title: Developer tools
pluginSettingGroups.description: 20 logo clicks unlock Dev-button; reopen the panel, enable Dev-mode separately and follow its restart prompt.

pluginSettingGroups.title: Developer MCP server
pluginSettingGroups.description: Visible only when Dev-mode is true. Enable defaults off. Open server folder, run start.bat or sh start.sh with Node 20+, and keep it running. Port/token/export live only in config.local.json; Pengu 1.1.6 reads it on disk, usable PluginFS also offers Settings read/write controls.

pluginSettingGroups.title: Retained legacy/background keys
pluginSettingGroups.description: Reference only, not current Settings controls. Auto Queue/Dodge are not started; other keys are retained internal or compatibility flags.

backupRestore.introduction: The Elaina Backup & Restore tab contains offline JSON controls first, then a separate cloud switch/status panel. Portable snapshots contain root-default keys, not arbitrary full datastore dumps.
storageModes: Without context.fs, ElainaData uses Pengu DataStore (ElainaTheme). With context.fs, it uses ./data/ElainaData.json.
Offline export/restore works without cloud access in either storage mode.
Only datastoreDefault.js keys are portable. API identity/tokens, caches, file-based MCP settings and runtime-only media lists/indices/progress are excluded.
MCP capture preferences are default-known keys and are included; config.local.json is not. Media files must be backed up separately.
manualBackup: Open Elaina theme -> Backup & Restore (not another plugin with the same tab title).
Click Backup/Sao lưu in the manual section.
Save ElainaTheme-<summonerId>.json, or ElainaTheme-local.json when no usable ID exists.
Keep a separate copy of custom media files and local server configuration if you intend to reinstall.
manualRestore: Open the manual section and click Restore/Khôi phục.
Select a .json backup. It is read/parsed once and filtered to recognized default keys.
Invalid/empty/non-object files do not partially apply. Credentials/current identity are preserved.
After values are applied and persistence confirmed, the client restarts after approximately two seconds. Wait until outside an active game before using restore.
cloudBackup: Cloud requires internet, current-account authentication, an available API and allowed backup-datastore consent.
Enable cloud backup only through available consent/settings UI; do not set consent flags to bypass a missing UI.
The panel reads existing cloud data when enabled. Theme close/restart hooks attempt uploads; crashes/force kills cannot guarantee a backup.
The live documentation survey returned HTTP 403; local JSON controls remained available. Use offline backup when the online path fails.
cloudRestore: Open Backup & Restore with cloud enabled and permitted.
Restore/Delete file are shown only after an existing backup is confirmed.
Restore applies recognized keys, flushes and schedules a restart; errors keep the current settings.

Delete removes the remote backup only after a confirmed API response. The underlying explicit-delete action can remain available after automatic uploads are disabled, but the current panel hides its buttons when cloud data is not loaded.
notes: System information is optional and fetched for the panel in Dev-mode; it must not block offline controls.
Portable backup filtering is key-based; do not treat it as complete per-key value/type validation.
The local helper requires privacy-consent-version and per-feature flags. It mentions Setup/privacy, but the current four-tab UI does not expose that tab or an own-icon upload switch.
Cloud/API consent is independent of Dev-mode/MCP. MCP disable does not stop the external Node service.
Request errors (including 401/403) are not proof that no backup exists; do not delete/reset data as a diagnostic.

faq.introduction: Common problems and the quickest checks for each one.

items.question: The theme does not appear in League Client settings.
answer: Verify that the built theme folder is inside the Pengu Loader plugins directory.
Verify that Pengu Loader is running and enabled for the League Client.
Restart the League Client.
Check the console for theme import or syntax errors.

items.question: My wallpaper or audio file does not show up.
answer: Verify the installed theme folder, basename and lowercase extension; accepted filenames still require a supported media codec.
With PluginFS, open/reopen Theme Settings or press the Home wallpaper dropdown. refreshLists scans all four lists; no always-running scan is active.
Without PluginFS, register the exact filename manually in Asset library, then leave/return Home to rebuild existing controls if necessary.
Restart is not required for PluginFS discovery and does not replace manual registration on legacy Pengu.

items.question: Settings are not saving.
answer: Check ElainaData storage mode rather than version alone. With PluginFS, verify read/write results for data/ElainaData.json; otherwise inspect the ElainaTheme DataStore entry.
Related values use setMany; flush confirms writes before restore/restart. Preserve a local backup before changing data files.
An MCP port/token save goes to config.local.json, not theme datastore or portable backups.

items.question: Auto Accept accepts too fast or accepts after I declined.
answer: Check `auto_accept_delay`; the value is in milliseconds and is capped by the plugin.
The current implementation cancels the pending accept when ReadyCheck ends or when your ready-check response becomes Declined.
If it still happens, disable Auto Accept button, reload the client, then re-enable it.

items.question: The client becomes slow after enabling wallpapers.
answer: Use smaller videos or image wallpapers.
Disable theme wallpaper or reduce video complexity.
Disable animated loading and other heavy visual replacements.
Reload the client after changing large assets.

items.question: Cloud backup says the server is unavailable.
answer: Check your internet connection.
Try again later; the cloud service may be sleeping or temporarily unavailable.
Use manual backup/restore when cloud backup is unavailable.

items.question: How do I reset the theme?
answer: Export a local backup and preserve media/configuration first.
A missing/empty PluginFS settings file can reimport legacy DataStore values, so deleting only that file may not create a clean reset.
Use a reviewed reset flow for the active backend; do not delete configuration or data simply to diagnose a network error.

items.question: Should I enable Developer mode?
answer: Keep it off for normal use. It selects local helper files and exposes diagnostics; those files must exist.
20 Plugins logo clicks unlock the developer controls, then Dev-mode is enabled separately.
MCP still defaults off and needs both Dev-mode and MCP-enabled. Turning either off disconnects/cancels capture and previews, but does not stop Node.

items.question: Does the Wallpaper/Audio save interval field still control playback writes?
answer: No. WallpaperAudio-timeUpdate remains visible with a runtime default of 3000 ms, but the code saves changed progress on page transition, pause and pagehide.
Audio/video share one setMany commit. There are no timeupdate/timer progress writes.

items.question: How do I connect Codex, Gemini or Claude to the developer MCP?
answer: Enable Dev-mode, open the MCP folder from Plugins Settings, run start.bat (Windows) or sh start.sh (macOS) with Node 20+, and enable MCP separately.
Use Streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp with the local bearer token, or node with mcp-server/dist/server/stdio.js. The adapter connects to the shared service.
Port/token/export live only in config.local.json. Restart Node after port/token changes; reconnect rereads the file.
The full package guide is in src/src/plugins/mcp-server/README.md in the source repository.

items.question: What is penguPluginsPath for?
answer: It is only the destination for export_plugin_to_pengu to save a live preview as a separate plugin.
An empty value disables export; DOM/log/click/screenshot access still works. It is not the theme source folder.

items.question: The API says to enable a feature in Setup / privacy, but that tab is missing.
answer: The current local helper requires per-feature consent plus privacy-consent-version; tracking also requires a reviewed-journal version.
The current settingsStructure.ts and surveyed UI register four Elaina tabs without Setup/privacy or an upload switch. This is a source/UI mismatch, not an instruction to bypass consent.
Use offline backup/local assets, record the helper/theme versions and update to a build with the corresponding consent UI when available. Download/upload icon permissions are independent.

items.question: Why do old Auto Queue/Dodge/TFT controls not appear or affect the current client?
answer: Auto Queue/Dodge/practice/skip-honor startup calls and the queue Settings section are commented out; stored keys are compatibility references.
TFT switches only target matching League renderer components. A separate TFT client launched from newer rcp-fe-tft is outside this theme renderer.

items.question: Do custom fonts need a client restart?
answer: Custom font local/Google modes are exclusive. Selecting a file, switching Google back to local or toggling custom font replaces the owned stylesheet immediately.
Verify the local filename or accepted Google CSS URL; follow restart prompts for other startup-dependent settings rather than applying a blanket restart rule.
